title: Aun cuando: una concesión más fuerte que aunque

sections.content: Aun cuando (even when, even though) is a stronger, more formal concession than aunque -- useful for emphasizing that something happened despite truly extreme or unexpected circumstances. It can take the indicative for a real, known situation or the subjunctive for a hypothetical one. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El gobierno negaba cualquier conocimiento de su paradero, aun cuando la familia había presenciado el propio arresto.
items.english: The government denied any knowledge of their whereabouts, even when the family had witnessed the arrest itself.

items.spanish: Las Madres de Plaza de Mayo siguieron marchando, aun cuando el régimen intentó reprimir sus protestas.
items.english: The Mothers of Plaza de Mayo kept marching, even when the regime tried to suppress their protests.

items.spanish: Aun cuando hizo desaparecer a algunas de sus propias fundadoras, el movimiento no dejó de exigir respuestas.
items.english: Even when it made some of its own founders disappear, the movement never stopped demanding answers.

items.spanish: Muchísimos casos permanecen sin resolver, aun cuando la desaparición forzada ya es reconocida como un crimen de lesa humanidad.
items.english: Countless cases remain unresolved, even though enforced disappearance is now recognized as a crime against humanity.

sections.content: Reach for aun cuando instead of aunque when the contrast you're describing is especially stark or surprising -- it carries more emphasis, closer to English even in the face of this than a plain even though.
